title: Experiments and memory
hired_for: So the business learns faster than it spends: every test has a hypothesis, a read date and a decision, nothing is tested twice, and winners get rolled out.

jobs.job: Get a clear decision out of every test: roll out, stop or run again
jobs.why: A test that ends with no decision cost traffic and money and taught nothing. The owner wants every closed test to end in one of three calls, written down with the reason.

watch.metric: share of closed tests with a recorded decision, trailing 90 days

drives.metric: gross profit banked from rolled-out winners, per month

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 6 of 14 tests closed in 90 days have no decision. After: 13 of 14 have one, and 4 winners are queued to roll out.

jobs.job: Read every test on the day we said we would
jobs.why: Late reads mean losing versions keep taking traffic and winners wait to ship. Every day a read slips costs sales on the weaker version.

watch.metric: share of tests read within 3 days of their read date, trailing 90 days

drives.metric: tests decided per month

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 5 reads are overdue, the oldest by 19 days. After: 90% of reads land within 3 days of the date set at launch.

jobs.job: Stop a losing test by the rule we set, not on one bad day
jobs.why: A losing version left running burns profit. A test stopped on one bad day throws away a result. The owner wants the stop rule set before launch and followed.

watch.metric: days a losing version ran past its stop rule, per month

drives.metric: gross profit lost in losing versions, per month

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 2 losing tests ran 11 days past their stop line, about $3,400 in lost profit. After: losers stop within 2 days of crossing the line.

jobs.job: Roll each winner out to the whole store and keep it live
jobs.why: A win that stays on half the traffic, or quietly gets undone by a theme update, earns nothing. The money only arrives when the winner is live for everyone.

watch.metric: share of winners live on 100% of traffic within 14 days of the read
watch.source: brand brain (experiment registry) checked against the live store

drives.metric: gross profit banked from rolled-out winners, per month

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 3 of 7 winners from last quarter are still on a 50% split. After: all 7 are live for everyone within 14 days.

jobs.job: Agree what winning and losing look like before a test starts
jobs.why: If the metric, the read date and the stop and scale rules are picked after the fact, any result can be spun. The owner wants one written hypothesis per test before launch.

watch.metric: share of running tests with hypothesis, main metric, read date and stop rule filled in

drives.metric: share of closed tests with a recorded decision

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 4 of 9 running tests have no read date. After: nothing launches until all 4 fields are filled.

jobs.job: Never pay to test the same idea twice
jobs.why: Without a record, the same idea comes back every year under a new name and costs another test window. The owner wants past results found before a repeat launches.

watch.metric: tests launched that repeat a past idea with no new reason, per quarter

drives.metric: test weeks spent on repeats

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 2 of 10 tests this quarter repeated old ideas. After: 0 repeats unless a reason is written, like a new product or new price.

jobs.job: Judge tests on gross profit, not clicks or revenue alone
jobs.why: A version that sells more at a deeper discount can lose money. The owner wants the winner picked on profit per visitor after product cost and discounts.

watch.metric: gross profit per visitor for each version, over the test window
watch.source: Shopify orders with product cost, GA4 sessions

drives.metric: gross profit banked from rolled-out winners

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: the last 3 wins were called on conversion rate; 1 of them lowered profit per visitor by 6%. After: every call shows profit per visitor side by side.

jobs.job: Put the next test on the biggest money leak first
jobs.why: Test slots are limited by traffic. Spending them on small ideas while a big leak runs costs the most money of all.

watch.metric: share of tests launched from the top 10 of the ranked list, per quarter

drives.metric: expected gross profit at stake per test launched

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 3 of 8 tests this quarter came from the top 10. After: 7 of 8 do, and the average test targets $9,000 a month at stake instead of $2,500.

jobs.job: Size each test so it can actually give an answer
jobs.why: A test with too few orders ends flat and wastes 4 weeks. The owner wants to know the orders needed and the days it will take before starting.

watch.metric: share of tests that reach their planned orders per version by the read date

drives.metric: share of tests with a readable result

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 5 of 12 tests ended short of the orders they needed. After: 11 of 12 reach their planned sample, or are not started.

jobs.job: Check a win did not raise returns, refunds or support tickets
jobs.why: A version that sells more but brings back more returns or angry tickets is not a win. The owner wants these side numbers checked before calling it.

watch.metric: return rate and refund rate of the winning version versus the other, 30 days after the read
watch.source: Shopify returns and refunds, Gorgias tickets

drives.metric: profit after returns and marketing

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: no win is checked for returns. After: every win shows return rate side by side; 1 of 6 wins is held back because returns rose 4 points.

jobs.job: Know what works for this brand, from our own past tests
jobs.why: General advice says what works for most stores. The owner wants the brand's own record for each idea, so the next bet starts from what happened here.

watch.metric: share of new proposals that show this brand's own past result for the idea

drives.metric: win rate of tests launched, trailing 12 months

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 0 of 20 proposals show a past result from this store. After: 8 of 20 do, and 2 repeat losers drop off the list.

jobs.job: Stop two tests from spoiling each other
jobs.why: Two tests on the same page, audience or dates blur each other, and both reads become useless. The owner wants clashes caught before launch.

watch.metric: running tests that share a page area, audience or date window

drives.metric: share of tests with a readable result

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 2 pairs of tests share the product page. After: 0 clashes, one of each pair moved 2 weeks later.

jobs.job: Check tracking works in both versions before a test goes live
jobs.why: If the purchase event fails in one version, or traffic splits unevenly, the result is wrong from day 1. A launch check saves a whole test window.

watch.metric: share of tests that passed the launch check: purchase fires in both versions and the traffic split is within 1 point of plan
watch.source: GA4 and Shopify orders by version

drives.metric: share of tests with a readable result

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 1 in 5 tests found a tracking gap after the read. After: every test passes the check in its first 2 days.

jobs.job: Ship the obvious fix instead of testing it
jobs.why: A broken button or a missing size chart does not need a 4-week test. Testing it wastes a slot and loses sales while it runs.

watch.metric: days from finding an obvious defect to fixing it

drives.metric: store conversion rate

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 3 plain fixes sit in the test queue for 3 weeks. After: fixes ship the same week and test slots go to real questions.

jobs.job: Keep promos and holidays out of test windows
jobs.why: A sale or holiday in the middle of a test changes who shops and why. The result then does not hold on a normal week.

watch.metric: tests whose window overlapped a sale, holiday or launch, per quarter
watch.source: brand brain (experiment registry and marketing calendar)

drives.metric: share of tests with a readable result

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 3 of 9 tests ran through a sale. After: tests are planned around the calendar and 0 overlap.

jobs.job: Show what the testing program earned in total, not the sum of wins
jobs.why: Adding up each test's lift overstates the gain. The owner wants one honest number: how much more profit per visitor the store makes than a group left on the old site.

watch.metric: gross profit per visitor, everyone versus a small group kept on the old site, 90 days

drives.metric: gross profit

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: the agency claims 38% total lift. After: the left-out group shows a real gain of 7% in profit per visitor.

jobs.job: Confirm winners still earn months later
jobs.why: Some wins fade as shoppers get used to them, or break after a site change. The owner wants past winners checked so the store is not coasting on old wins.

watch.metric: shipped winners still live and still ahead at 90 days

drives.metric: gross profit banked from rolled-out winners

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: nobody knows if 12 past winners are still live. After: a quarterly check finds 2 broken and 1 faded; all 3 are fixed or reverted.

jobs.job: Run as many tests as the traffic can carry, and no more
jobs.why: Too few tests and the store learns slowly. Too many and none reach an answer. The owner wants the pace matched to real orders.

watch.metric: tests completed per month versus the most the store's orders can power

drives.metric: gross profit banked per quarter

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 1 test a month on traffic that could carry 3. After: 3 a month, each on a different page area.

jobs.job: Record why a result could not be read, and fix the gap
jobs.why: A read with missing data is not a zero. It must be named as unreadable, with the missing field, so it gets fixed before the next test.

watch.metric: share of reads marked unreadable, with the missing field named, trailing 90 days

drives.metric: share of tests with a recorded decision

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 3 reads were quietly called flat when purchase data was missing. After: they show as unreadable with the cause, and the next 5 tests read clean.

jobs.job: Write down what we learned after every test and project
jobs.why: If the learning lives in one person's head, it leaves with them. The owner wants one line per test: what worked, what did not, would we do it again.

watch.metric: share of closed tests and projects with a written learning

drives.metric: tests launched that repeat a past idea with no new reason

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 4 of 15 closed tests have a learning note. After: 15 of 15 do, filed within 7 days of close.

jobs.job: Bring parked ideas back when the reason to wait runs out
jobs.why: Good ideas get parked for a reason, like low stock or a busy season. When that reason ends, they should come back, not be forgotten.

watch.metric: parked ideas past their review date with no new decision

drives.metric: expected gross profit in the ranked list

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 7 parked ideas are past their date. After: 0 are, and 2 go back into the ranked list this month.

jobs.job: Stop making me repeat the same reason to say no
jobs.why: When the owner rejects the same kind of idea 3 times for the same reason, the list should learn. Repeating it wastes the owner's time every week.

watch.metric: share of top 10 proposals rejected for a reason already given 3 or more times

drives.metric: tests approved per week

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 3 of each week's top 10 get rejected for 'no discounts'. After: 0 do; ideas like that rank lower on their own.

jobs.job: Set a fair win rate so a flat month is not called a failure
jobs.why: Most store tests do not win. If the owner expects every test to win, the program gets cut just before it pays off.

watch.metric: win rate of closed tests, trailing 90 days, against the expected range

drives.metric: tests run per quarter

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 2 wins in 12 tests reads as failure. After: the page shows 17% against an expected 10 to 20%, and the program keeps its budget.

jobs.job: Judge a testing agency by profit proven, not tests run
jobs.why: Agencies often report test count and summed lifts. The owner wants to know what each dollar of fees brought back.

watch.metric: gross profit banked from rolled-out winners per dollar of agency fees, per quarter
watch.source: brand brain (experiment registry and vendor fees), Shopify

drives.metric: return on testing fees

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: the agency reports 22 tests and 41% total lift. After: $1.80 of banked profit per $1 of fees, shown next to the fee.

jobs.job: Hand a new hire or agency the reasons behind past decisions
jobs.why: When a person or agency changes, the reasons behind past tests are lost and old mistakes come back. The owner wants the history handed over in one place.

watch.metric: areas with an up-to-date decision history export in the last 90 days

drives.metric: days from a new person starting to their first test launched

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: a new agency spent 5 weeks relearning what had been tested. After: they get the full history on day 1 and launch a test in week 2.
